key_insights: Asia saw broad pressure across the AI complex on 16 Nov 2026: Taiwan -6%, Korea -3.6%, Nikkei -2.4%, with Advantest -11%, Lasertec -9%, Tokyo Electron -7%, Hynix -7.81% and TSMC -5.7%. Japan domestic consumer names rose +2.75% and healthcare +1.75%, while Japan beta fell -3.97% and high beta momentum -2.81%.

Privorotsky says the market treated last week's Nvidia news as a tactical redistribution of hardware market share. He thinks the larger question is the duration of the whole AI capex cycle, and whether this is a rotation or the start of a digestion phase in aggregate AI enterprise capex.
Nominal Treasury yields rose by multiple sigma last week and all three Treasury auctions reportedly tailed, which signals weak demand for duration. A tamer PPI made no difference to the selloff.

Credit has held up well despite the rate move. Privorotsky's read is 'less spending, better credit, weaker equity multiples': reduced AI commitments could hurt equity growth expectations but help credit as balance sheet risk falls.

GS prime book: fundamental strategies were up just over 1% and quant about 1.5% last week. Fundamental performance was mostly beta driven and quant performance was alpha driven. Fundamental L/S gross leverage rose 2.6 pts (34th percentile, 1yr) with nets barely changed, while overall PB gross fell 2 pts, with visible de-grossing in Asia and Europe.

US flows were dominated by single stock shorting, partly offset by ETF covering. Hedge funds were net sellers of US equities for a 2nd straight week (5 of the last 6). ETF shorts fell 8.6%, the largest covering in seven months.

Tape is rotational: beta and momentum are falling while low vol and quality are bid. Parts of semiconductors are near historical valuation lows while consumer staples trade at large forward-earnings premiums. Privorotsky says he is struggling to square the two.

Defensives would make sense if nominal and real yields were falling with growth, but they are not. Equities are pricing a slowdown while rates are pricing persistent inflation and restrictive policy. He asks whether receiving rates is the better expression.

Sentiment is depressed, with the AAII bull/bear indicator near the low end of its range and CNN fear/greed similar but only beginning to recover. Positioning is the saving grace and likely drove last week's squeeze, but with AI leadership under pressure, expensive defensives and no relief from rates, he sees no clear driver of a sustained recovery.

UK: Burnham speaks ahead of the UK/EU summit, with the reset focused on trade, carbon markets and youth mobility. The Milburn review puts youth inactivity and welfare reform back in focus, but benefits will take time. Employment and CPI are the immediate catalysts, against weak growth and employment with stubborn inflation.

France: the social security financing bill faces a Senate vote Wednesday after its National Assembly rejection. For OATs the issue is whether any credible fiscal adjustment survives the parliamentary process, not the vote itself.

Week ahead: Nvidia earnings Tuesday are unlikely to resolve the future AI commitments debate. They probably reinforce that the stock is heavily discounted on next year's numbers, while the correct multiple for 2028+ is unknowable.

tension_points.bear_case: The real issue may be the duration of the whole AI capex cycle, with aggregate enterprise capex entering a digestion phase and equity growth expectations falling.
